children: Routing Items To Inbound Quality Control (RF & Non-RF)

Below is a discussion of how the system will route a particular item 
 quantity from a receipt to an inbound quality control location. If an item is defined 
 to require quality control inspection (on the item master), the system 
 will have the option of routing it to a QC location after the check in 
 action is performed. The system will initiate this by displaying a window 
 that shows how much of the quantity being checked in will be routed to 
 a quality control location versus a standard storage location. The user 
 can then choose to have the system divert the required quantity to QC, 
 or cancel the check in request.

The system will only check each receipt once 
 for QC-eligible items. So, if you partially check in an item quantity 
 that does not meet the full inspection quantity that is expected, the 
 system will not check any further item quantities that you check in for 
 this receipt. On the next receipt that includes this item, the system 
 will check for the full QC inspection quantity again.
Keep in mind that inbound quality control only supports license plates created by the check in process, not downloaded receipt containers.
Setup Prerequisites for This Topic's Examples...

The receiving preference for the quality control 
 flag is set to active.

The item (CMP-01) 
 that you are receiving is QC eligible, and is slated to have 5 eaches 
 inspected from each incoming receipt.

There is not already a checked in container for 
 item CMP-01 that is currently 
 participating in quality control.
Discussion: How the System Computes the QC Item Quantity...

The amount that the system will route to quality control is defined 
 on the item master. This can either be a raw amount (for example, 50 eaches, 
 2 cases, etc), or a percentage value (for example, 5 percent of the total 
 item quantity on each receipt that the warehouse receives).

If the configured 
 QC amount is a discrete amount the system will convert it to the 
 lowest unit of measure. If the user does not choose a UM, the system will 
 treat the number as being in the lowest unit of measure.

If the QC amount 
 is a percentage the system will compute the quantity by applying 
 the percentage against the total open quantity on the receipt for that 
 item. The system will also convert this to the lowest unit of measure.

The system will then make some additional calculations in order to avoid 
 sending an inappropriate quantity to quality control (such as 2.67 cases 
 or 1.23 pallets). The system will take the amount it computed for the 
 base UM above, and obtain the UM that is the second from the top increment 
 in your storage template (for example, a case 
 in an each-case-pallet hierarchy). 
 Then, the system will take the original quantity (computed with the base 
 UM) and round it down to the next whole increment of the new UM. If the 
 quantity is not large enough to complete 1 whole increment of this unit 
 of measure, the system will simply leave it in the base UM and not perform 
 any rounding. The system will indicate that it has made special rounding 
 calculations on the QC Inspection Verification Window.

For example (assume the each-case-pallet hierarchy; 20 pieces per case and 5 cases per pallet, which would make case the UM that the system would 
 use for rounding):
10 EA (would not round down to 0 cases)
The following examples illustrate the process outlines above:

Your warehouse 
 receives in 50 EA of item CMP-01

A receiving dock 
 user checks in the full item quantity of item  CMP-01 (50) in the Receipt Workbench. 
 As a result of the settings for this item on the item master, the system 
 will want to route a quantity of 5 of item CMP-01 to a quality control 
 location. The system then will display the QC Inspection Verification 
 screen. Any additional rounding calculations that 
 the system needs to make will also be indicated in this window.

If the user chooses OK 
 the system will compare the quality control inspection amount versus the 
 total amount of the item being checked in. Then, the system will split 
 this item quantity into two check in requests. Below are the three scenarios 
 depending on the quantity being checked in:

a) If the inspection amount     IS 
 LESS THAN the checked in amount, the system will split off the 
 inspection amount quantity. This is the correct scenario for this example; 
 when the user locates the quantity, the system would split off 5 eaches 
 for so it can be routed to a quality control location. The remaining quantity 
 (45 eaches) will be checked in and as normal.

b) If the inspection amount     IS 
 GREATER THAN the checked 
 in amount,when the user locates 
 the quantity, the system will route the entire item quantity to the quality 
 control location. As a result, the checked in amount does not meet the 
 requested inspection amount. In our example, this scenario would have 
 been correct if the total checked in quantity had been less than 5 eaches, 
 not 50.

c) If the inspection amount     IS 
 EQUAL TO the checked in 
 amount, when the user locates the quantity, the system will route the 
 entire item quantity to quality control. In our example, this scenario 
 would have been correct if the total checked in quantity had been 5 eaches 
 exactly, not 50.If the user chooses Cancel 
 the system will return you to the Receipt Workbench without checking 
 in the item quantity.

A receiving dock 
 RF user checks in the full item quantity of item  CMP-01 (50) on the RF's Check In Screen. As 
 a result of the settings for this item on the item master, the system 
 will want to route a quantity of 5 of item CMP-01 to a quality control 
 location. The system then will display the QC Inspection Screen, which 
 will show the "inspection" amount and the "checked in" 
 amount of the item quantity.

Choose to confirm/not 
 confirm the check in action:

If the user chooses OK 
 the system will compare the quality control inspection amount versus the

a) If the inspection amount      IS

 in amount, the system will split off the inspection amount quantity. This

 the system would split off 5 eaches for so it can be routed to a quality 
 control location. The remaining quantity (45 eaches) will be checked in 
 and as normal.

b) If the inspection amount      IS 
 GREATER THAN  the checked 
 in amount,when the user locates 
 the quantity, the system will route the entire item quantity to the quality 
 control location. As a result, the checked in amount does not meet the

c) If the inspection amount      IS
